title: Convert Stripe Payouts to QuickBooks Online
metaDescription: Convert your Stripe payout reconciliation report into a QuickBooks Online journal-entry import and a matching bank-reconciliation file. No signup, no subscription.
painPoint: Stripe bundles dozens of charges, refunds, and fees into a single payout deposit — and that one bank-feed line never matches anything in QuickBooks, so you're stuck either fudging a manual deposit or picking through fees one at a time.
howToExport: In your Stripe Dashboard, go to Balance → Payouts
Click the payout you want to reconcile
Click “Download reconciliation report” and save the CSV

title: Convert Stripe Payouts to Xero
metaDescription: Convert your Stripe payout reconciliation report into a Xero manual journal import and a matching bank statement file. No signup, no subscription.
painPoint: Xero's bank feed shows one lump Stripe deposit, but your actual sales, refunds, and processing fees are buried inside it — reconciling by hand means re-deriving the split every single payout.
howToExport: In your Stripe Dashboard, go to Balance → Payouts
Click the payout you want to reconcile
Click “Download reconciliation report” and save the CSV

title: Convert PayPal Transactions to QuickBooks Online
metaDescription: Convert your PayPal activity export into a QuickBooks Online journal-entry import and a matching bank-reconciliation file. No signup, no subscription.
painPoint: PayPal's activity export has the right numbers (gross, fee, net) but not a QuickBooks-importable shape — so every transaction gets typed in or fudged by hand, fees and all.
howToExport: In PayPal, go to Activity → Statements → Download Statements
Choose “Activity download”, CSV format, and your date range

title: Stripe Payout Doesn't Match QuickBooks? Here's the Fix
metaDescription: Stripe payout won't match your QuickBooks bank feed? Convert it into a clean, single-line bank-match file plus the underlying journal entries.
painPoint: QuickBooks Online can't natively split a bundled Stripe payout into the sale, the fee, and the net deposit — QuickBooks' own support staff routinely point people at a manual “Resolve Difference” workaround because there's no built-in fix.
howToExport: In your Stripe Dashboard, go to Balance → Payouts
Click the payout you want to reconcile
Click “Download reconciliation report” and save the CSV

title: Fix Duplicate Stripe Fees in QuickBooks
metaDescription: Stop double-counting Stripe processing fees in QuickBooks. Convert your payout report into a journal entry that books gross, fee, and net exactly once.
painPoint: Auto-matching a Stripe deposit against individual invoices in QuickBooks often creates duplicate fee entries — the fee gets booked once by the matcher and again by whatever process created the original invoice.
howToExport: In your Stripe Dashboard, go to Balance → Payouts
Click the payout you want to reconcile
Click “Download reconciliation report” and save the CSV
